sentences.text:
The petitioner has filed this petition being aggrieved by the arbitral award passed by the Special Deputy Commissioner/Arbitrator, Bengaluru Urban District, Bengaluru, in No.
LAQ/ARB/NH-7/CR/194/2012-13 dated 21.09.2021 pertaining to Sy. No.99 measuring 147 Sq.
Meters of Yelahanka village.

.2. The definite case of the petitioner is that the property measuring 147 Sq. Meters in Sy. No.99 of Yelahanka village has A.P. No.43/2022 been acquired under Preliminary Notification issued by the respondent No. 3 under Section 3A(1) vide S.O. No.3159(E) dated 09.12.2009 and Final Notification under Section 3D(1) and (2) vide S.O. No.1874(E) dated 30.07.2010.
The respondent No.3 has passed the award on 02.04.2011 and determined the market value of agricultural lands at Rs.2,75,00,000/- per acre and that of NA lands at Rs.1,389/- per Sq. feet.
The respondent No.3 has passed the award on 02.04.2011 and awarded a total compensation amount of Rs.9,98,937/-, which has been received by the respondent No.1 under protest.

Subsequently, on 29.11.2012 the respondent No.1 has filed the application for enhancing the compensation at the rate of Rs.10,000/-
per Sq. feet.
Accordingly, the application is taken by the respondent No.2 for consideration.
. 3 . T h e r e a f t e r , t h e A r b i t r a t o r h o l d a n i n q u i r y a n d p a s s e d o r d e r i n

.4. Being aggrieved by the impugned Arbitral Award, the petitioner filed this petition under Section 34(2) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, setting aside the following:
A.P. No.43/2022 :GROUNDS:
The petitioner claims that the impugned award passed by the respondent No.2 is perverse, patently illegal, capricious and goes against the fundamentals of Arbitration and Conciliation Act.
The impugned arbitral award is completely illegal and arbitrary and without according any reasons.

The respondent No.2 while completely ignoring Section 3-G(7)(a) of the NH Act, has placed reliance upon the aforesaid notification has observed that the guidance value of NA lands situated at Yelahanka village as

Rs.
3,000/- per Sq. feet.

As per the notification dated 21.09.2011, the addition to be made on the guidance value @ 50% for the lands abutting NH and @ 25% for the lands National Highway Authority Of India vs Lakshmamma K S on 4 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/183923299/

sentences.text: 2 abutting State Highway for which lands rates have not been fixed specifically
. There are manifest errors in the impugned Arbitral Award and consequently the same is liable to be set aside under Section 34(2A) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act Act.

The respondent No.2 has not at all taken the trouble of independently conducting an inquiry into the market value of the subject lands as on the date of Preliminary Notification and the respondent No.2 has given A.P. No.43/2022 the benefit of enhancement to the respondent No. 1 without production of any documentary or oral evidence by the respondent No. 1.
It is also claimed by the petitioner that the impugned Arbitral Award was passed on 21.09.2021 and certified copy of the same was received on 18.10.2021.
The stipulated period of 3 months commences from the date of receipt of the impugned Arbitral Award and expired on 18.01.2022.
But the Hon'ble Supreme Court vide its order dated 10.01.2022 has excluded the period from 15.03.2020 till 28.02.2022 for the purpose of calculating limitation.
Hence, the petition is in time and among grounds, prayed for relief claimed in the petition.

.5. The respondent No. 1 to 3 though served with the notice, the respondent No.1 appeared before the Court through her advocate and the respondents 2 an 3 not chosen to appear before this Court to resist the petition and hence, they were placed exparte.
The entire records in LAQ/ARB/NH-7/CR/197/2012-13 secured from the Arbitrator.

On the basis of above, the points for consideration are as under:
1) Whether the impugned award of the Arbitrator/SLAO is against law, fact, evidence and probabilities of the case and liable to be intervened by this Court?
2) What order or award?
.7. Heard the arguments.

The petitioner has produced the citation reported in Karnataka Judicial Employees House Building Co-operative Society Vs. The State and others - ILR 1997 KAR 3419; (2)
Oil & Natural Gas Corp. Ltd Vs. SAW Pipes Ltd - AIR 2003 SC 2629); (3) Ssangyong Engineering &
Construction Co, Ltd Vs. NHAI - AIR 2019 SC 5041; (4) Som Dutt Builders Vs. State of Kerala - (2009)10 SCC 259; and (5) The order dated 10 th January 2022 passed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court extending the period of limitation.

Perused the materials on record, on that basis my findings on the above points are as under:
Point No.1 : In the Affirmative Point No.2 : As per final order, for the following:
A.P. No.43/2022 REASONS .8. POINT No.1:
Before proceeding further in this case, it is relevant to note the admitted and undisputed facts of this case.

The respondent No.1 is the owner of the land in Sy. No.99 measuring to an extent of 147 Sq. Meters situated at Yelahanka village and the said property has been acquired for widening of NH-7 under Preliminary Notification dated 09.12.2009 and Final Notification dated 30.07.2010 is an admitted fact.

It is also an admitted and undisputed fact in this case National Highway Authority Of India vs Lakshmamma K S on 4 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/183923299/
3 that the respondent No.3/Special Land Acquisition and Competent Authority of National Highways Authority of India being a SLAO determined the compensation at Rs.2,75,00,000/- per acre and that of NA lands at Rs. 1,389/- per Sq. feet for the acquired land.

sentences.text: It is also admitted and undisputed fact that awarded compensation of Rs. 9,98,937/- has been disbursed to the respondent No.1 as compensation.

.9. Subsequent to the receipt of compensation or passing of the award, the respondent No.1 filed an application on 29.11.2012 before the respondent No.2 claiming that they are entitled for compensation at the rate of Rs.10,000/-per Sq.
feet.

On the basis A.P. No.43/2022 of the said application, the respondent No.2 hold an inquiry and passed order in LAQ/ARB/NH-7/CR/194/2012-13,14/2013-14,
47/2011-12 dated 21.09.2021.
.10.
The said enhancement has been challenged by the petitioner in this petition.

The grievance of the petitioner is that the respondent No.2 without considering the relevant provisions of NHA Act and also without considering the guidance value or market value of the property as on the date of Preliminary Notification enhanced the compensation by relying on the guidance value of the year 2009 published vide notification bearing No. CVC-19/2010-11 dated 21.09.2011 and the said document is not part of arbitration proceedings.
The petitioner also claimed the Preliminary Notification dated 09.12.2009.

As such, the respondent No.2 ought to have considered the market value of the land of the year 2009 and not of the year 2011 as the aforesaid notification relied by the Arbitrator came to effect from 2011 i.e., after lapse of more than a year from the date of publication of Preliminary Notification.
Accordingly claimed that the said enhancement cannot be accepted.
It is true that as per A.P. No.43/2022 the NH Act, the market value of the land as on the date of Preliminary Notification has to be considered.

.11. The petitioner also claimed that whatever the document relied by the respondent No.2 for enhancing the compensation is not brought to the notice of the petitioner before passing the award/judgment.
Accordingly, claimed that such award is liable to be set aside as per Section 24 of National Highways Authority Act.
In this context, the petitioner relied on the decision reported in (2019) 15 SCC 131 in a case of Ssangyong Engineering and Construction Company Limited Vs. National Highways Authority of India.

entities.text: Ssangyong Engineering and Construction Company Limited Vs. National Highways Authority of India
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is true that in the said decision, the Hon'ble Supreme Court held that whatever the document relied by the Arbitrator shall be brought to the notice of the parties, so that the parties can make submission or give a rebuttal evidence about such documents.
However, in the case on hand, such notification is not found in the record received from the Arbitrator.

In the case on hand, the Arbitrator has enhanced compensation to Rs. 3000/- per square feet from Rs.631/- per square feet on the basis notification subsequent to the preliminary notification as aforesaid.

As discussed earlier, the preliminary notification is A.P. No.43/2022 dated 09-12-2009 and the Arbitrator relied on the notification bearing No.CVC/19/2010-11 dated 21-09-2011 and the said notification itself is published subsequent to the award National Highway Authority Of India vs Lakshmamma K S on 4 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/183923299/
4 passed by the LAO.

entities.text: National Highway Authority Of India vs Lakshmamma K S
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The LAO/respondent No.3 passed the award as on 02- 04-2011.
Whatever the enhancement has been granted by the Arbitrator, certainly effect the State or State Exchequer.
Hence, Arbitrator shall give reasons for enhancement of the compensation.

As already stated above, the Arbitrator / respondent No.2 has not given any explanation for enhancement except relying on the notification bearing No.CVC/19/2010-11 dated 21-09-2011 which is not the part of arbitration proceedings and the same is not brought to the notice of petitioner before passing the award.
Hence such enhancement cannot be accepted.

.12. In the case on hand, though the respondent No.2 and 3 served with the notice not chosen to appear before the court to resist the case of the petitioner or to support the award passed by the respondent No.2.
Absolutely there is no material placed before the court to disbelieve the petitioner case or to substantiate the award passed by the respondent No.2.

Hence, this Court is of the humble opinion that the petitioner has made out sufficient A.P. No.43/2022 grounds to intervene with the award passed by the Arbitrator and the award is liable to be set aside.
Accordingly, the point No. 1 is held in the affirmative.
.13. Point No.2:
In view of my above finding, I proceed to pass the following.
ORDER Petition is allowed.

Consequently, the award passed by the Arbitrator / respondent No.2 in case No. LAQ / ARB / NH-7 / CR / 194 / 2012-13 dated 21.09.2021 pertaining to Sy. No.99 measuring 147 Sq. Meters of Yelahanka village, Yelahanka Hobli, Bengaluru North Taluka is set aside.
